supersedes.reason: Steps 14 and 14B changed the learner experience: the lesson went from 6 chapters to 9, gained a universal Explore system and a retrieval challenge, and gained narration for all of it. The Step-13 package describes a build that is no longer the candidate. It is retained unchanged as the record of what was frozen then.

validatedProceduralRig: elbow_r (right elbow, hinge) - single DOF flexion, fitted axis, 0-145 deg approximate teaching range
validatedVsSchematic.enforcement: checkExploreConfigs() refuses a group-driven exploration that declares itself a validated rig; the status is on screen for as long as an exploration is open; every schematic indicator carries a note.

shots.caption: Types of Joints / How different joints allow different kinds of movement.
shots.narration: Types of Joints. How different joints allow different kinds of movement.
shots.screenReader: A full human skeleton inside a faint outline of the body, seen from the front.

shots.caption: Your shoulder can swing your arm in almost any direction.
shots.note: Schematic indicator: it shows the kind of movement only. This part of the body is not animated.
shots.narration: Your shoulder can swing your arm in almost any direction.
shots.screenReader: The right shoulder, seen from the front and right. Curved arrows around the top of the upper arm bone show movement in many directions.

shots.caption: Your elbow mainly bends and straightens.
shots.note: Schematic indicator: it shows the kind of movement only. This part of the body is not animated.
shots.narration: Your elbow mainly bends and straightens.
shots.screenReader: The right elbow, seen from the side. An arc shows the forearm bending in one direction.

shots.caption: Both are joints. So why do they move so differently?
shots.note: Schematic indicator: it shows the kind of movement only. This part of the body is not animated.
shots.narration: Both are joints. So why do they move so differently?
shots.screenReader: The whole skeleton, with the shoulder and elbow indicators still moving.

shots.caption: A joint is a place where two bones meet.
shots.narration: A joint is a place where two bones meet.
shots.screenReader: Close view of the right elbow, where the upper arm bone meets the two forearm bones.

shots.caption: The way the bones meet decides how they can move.
shots.note: Schematic indicator: it shows the kind of movement only. This part of the body is not animated.
shots.narration: The way the bones meet decides how they can move.
shots.screenReader: The head, the top of the neck and the right shoulder together, each with its own movement indicator.

shots.caption: You have joints like these all over your body. We will look at four kinds.
shots.narration: You have joints like these all over your body. We will look at four kinds.
shots.screenReader: The camera turns slightly. The skull, neck, right shoulder, right hip, right elbow and right knee are softly highlighted.

shots.caption: Fixed joint
shots.narration: Fixed joint.
shots.screenReader: The camera moves up to the skull. The skull bones are highlighted.

shots.caption: The bones of the skull meet at fixed joints. These bones do not move against each other.
shots.note: Schematic indicator: it shows the kind of movement only. This part of the body is not animated.
shots.narration: The bones of the skull meet at fixed joints. These bones do not move against each other.
shots.screenReader: Side view of the skull. The frontal and right parietal bones are highlighted where they meet; a dashed ring marks a fixed joint.

shots.caption: Pivot joint
shots.narration: Pivot joint.
shots.screenReader: The camera moves down to the top of the neck. The first two neck vertebrae are highlighted.

shots.caption: Where the skull meets the backbone, a pivot joint lets the head turn around an axis.
shots.note: Schematic indicator: it shows the kind of movement only. This part of the body is not animated.
shots.narration: Where the skull meets the backbone, a pivot joint lets the head turn around an axis.
shots.screenReader: An arrow circles around a vertical line at the top of the neck, showing turning.

shots.caption: Ball-and-socket joint
shots.narration: Ball-and-socket joint.
shots.screenReader: The camera moves to the right shoulder. The upper arm bone and shoulder blade are highlighted.

shots.caption: At the shoulder, the rounded top of the upper arm bone sits in a hollow of the shoulder bone, so the arm can move in many directions.
shots.note: Schematic indicator: it shows the kind of movement only. This part of the body is not animated.
shots.narration: At the shoulder, the rounded top of the upper arm bone sits in a hollow of the shoulder bone, so the arm can move in many directions.
shots.screenReader: Two curved arrows around the head of the upper arm bone show movement in many directions.

shots.caption: The hip is another ball-and-socket joint.
shots.note: Schematic indicator: it shows the kind of movement only. This part of the body is not animated.
shots.narration: The hip is another ball-and-socket joint.
shots.screenReader: The camera moves down to the right hip, where similar arrows show many directions of movement.

shots.caption: Hinge joint
shots.narration: Hinge joint.
shots.screenReader: The camera moves to the right elbow.

shots.caption: The elbow bends and straightens in one direction, similar to a door hinge.
shots.narration: The elbow bends and straightens in one direction, similar to a door hinge.
shots.screenReader: Side view of the right elbow, highlighted.

shots.caption: At the elbow, the humerus meets the radius and the ulna.
shots.narration: At the elbow, the humerus meets the radius and the ulna.
shots.screenReader: Close-up of the elbow. The humerus, radius and ulna are highlighted and labelled.

shots.caption: The forearm turns around one line: the hinge axis.
shots.note: Blue line: the hinge axis fitted to this 3D model.
shots.narration: The forearm turns around one line: the hinge axis.
shots.screenReader: A blue line through the elbow shows the hinge axis. The forearm straightens to 0 degrees.

shots.caption: Bending the elbow is called flexion.
shots.narration: Bending the elbow is called flexion.
shots.screenReader: The forearm bends around the axis from 0 to 45 and then 90 degrees. An orange arc shows the angle.

shots.caption: Straightening it again is called extension.
shots.note: 0-145 deg is an approximate teaching range for this model; adult elbow flexion varies between people (see Sources).
shots.narration: Straightening it again is called extension.
shots.screenReader: The forearm bends further to 145 degrees and then straightens back to 0 degrees.

shots.caption: Your turn: bend and straighten the elbow.
shots.narration: Your turn: bend and straighten the elbow. Drag the forearm to bend the elbow.
shots.screenReader: The elbow can be bent by dragging the forearm or with the slider.

shots.caption: Try it: bend the elbow to about 90°.
shots.narration: Try it: bend the elbow to about 90°.
shots.screenReader: Close-up of the elbow with its angle shown, ready to be bent to about 90 degrees.

shots.caption: A joint capsule and ligaments surround the elbow.
shots.note: The thin coloured lines are schematic ligament bands, not real tissue.
shots.narration: A joint capsule and ligaments surround the elbow.
shots.screenReader: The joint capsule and ligaments appear around the elbow, with two thin schematic bands.
The elbow returns to its resting position.

shots.caption: The knee is another hinge joint.
shots.note: Schematic indicator: it shows the kind of movement only. This part of the body is not animated.
shots.narration: The knee is another hinge joint.
shots.screenReader: The camera moves down to the right knee, where an arc shows bending in one direction.

shots.caption: Four joints. Four different ways of moving.
shots.narration: Four joints. Four different ways of moving.
shots.screenReader: The camera pulls back to the whole body.

explores.title: Fixed joint · skull
explores.instruction: Try to move the skull bones.
explores.explanation: These bones barely move. A fixed joint holds bones firmly together.

explores.title: Pivot joint · top of the neck
explores.instruction: Drag left and right to turn the head.
explores.explanation: The head turns around the bone below it. A pivot joint allows rotation.

explores.title: Ball-and-socket joint · shoulder
explores.instruction: Drag in any direction to move the arm.
explores.explanation: The arm moves in many directions, not just one. That is a ball-and-socket joint.

explores.title: Hinge joint · elbow
explores.instruction: Drag to bend and straighten the elbow.
explores.explanation: The elbow bends and straightens in one direction, like a door hinge.

steps.question: These skull bones hardly move at all.
steps.reveal: Fixed: the bones hold firm, so there is little or no movement.

steps.question: The head turns around the bone below it.
steps.reveal: Pivot: one bone rotates around another.

steps.question: The arm moves in many directions.
steps.reveal: Ball-and-socket: the rounded end sits in a socket, so it moves many ways.

steps.question: This joint bends and straightens in one direction.
steps.reveal: Hinge: it bends and straightens in one main direction.

steps.question: This joint in the leg bends and straightens one way.
steps.reveal: Hinge: the knee bends and straightens, like the elbow.

integrity.note: Nothing in this list was modified to produce this record. Hashes identify exactly what the expert is reviewing.
integrity.reviewCapturesNote: qa/visual/ is git-ignored by repository policy because every capture set is reproducible from its own script. These 69 captures are reproduced by qa/expert/step15/capture_review_set.mjs (tracked, and hashed in packageFiles) against the built dist of this candidate; the SHA-256 of each one is recorded above, so a reviewer who regenerates them can verify they are looking at the same images. To send the package to an off-machine reviewer, ship qa/visual/step15/ alongside it.

howToUse: Open reviewer-checklist.md and work through it with the captures in qa/visual/step15/. Record every decision in expert-review-status.json. A passing automated test is evidence, not approval: no item may be moved off PENDING because a test passed.
